You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Nozzle: 0.4 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA (high-speed PLA, black)
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm
- Supports: none. Every part has to print without them.

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## Their own parts
The person has these too, for this design only. Refer to each by its reference, such as "own:led-disk". What isn't listed hasn't been measured: ask them.

```yaml
- ref: own:led-disk
  kind: board
  description: 'Adafruit DotStar RGB LED Disk, product 2477 (Soya LED SY-C255-102): 255 APA102C LEDs on a round, rigid white circuit board, with its input wires on a 4-pin connector'
  frame: origin at the centre of the board's back face (the side without LEDs); +z out through the LED side; +y towards where its input wires leave
- ref: own:perfboard
  kind: board
  description: their perfboard, with an ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 (N16R8) plugged into female headers, screw terminals and a capacitor soldered on, and four wires running to the disk's input; it has four holes, one in each corner
  frame: origin at the centre of the board's top face (the side the ESP32 is on); +z up from that face; +y along the board's long side
- ref: own:esp32
  kind: board
  description: the ESP32 on the perfboard; a USB-C wall charger plugs straight into its own USB-C port to power the light
  frame: origin at the centre of the mouth of the ESP32's USB-C port; +x straight out of the port, the way a plug's cable leaves it; +z up from the ESP32's top face; y along the mouth's long side
- ref: own:m2x6-self-tapping
  kind: screw
  description: M2 x 6 self-tapping screws
  d: 2
  length: 6
```

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- print_test(params, parts): optional. If you need to know whether something is going to work but you're not sure, ask the person to print a test of it before you hand in the final design, so you both save time and filament. They print it and tell you how each piece came out.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 12 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.
- Say where each final part and each of their own parts with a frame goes in the finished piece, and where each screw goes, in `assembly`.

I'm making a round light to hang on my wall: an Adafruit DotStar LED disc, the 255-LED one. I'll 3D print the front and sides in transparent PLA, so they look frosted and you can't make out the diodes, and the box behind the disc in matte white. The front and sides come later: for now I only need that box, with the disc screwed onto it. Inside it is an ESP32 on a perfboard, with four wires from the perfboard to the disc. The disc screws onto the front of the box with M3 screws, through two small holes near its centre. The holes aren't on its datasheet. The box hangs flat against the wall on two screws, and I power it with a USB-C charger plugged straight into the ESP32, so I need to reach its port from outside once it's all closed up.

reasoning:
I'm working out the hole centres first: the inner edges are 30.2 mm apart and the holes are 3.3 mm wide, so the centre-to-centre spacing is 33.5 mm. The 102.54 figure for the disc edge looks odd since it's larger than the radius, so I'm guessing it means the far edge of the disc measured from the outside of one hole, which puts the hole's outer edge about 18.4 mm from its centre.

Working backwards, 84.1 radius would give a 168 mm disc, which doesn't fit the numbers, so I'm checking against the Adafruit 255 LED DotStar disk I vaguely recall at about 240 mm. Adding the two 102 figures to the hole spacing gives roughly 241.6 mm, which matches that diameter and puts the hole centres within about 0.15 mm of where they should be. That suggests the box behind the disc doesn't have to match the disc size, but I'm wondering whether making it the full disc diameter would make attaching the sides easier.

I'm thinking the box behind the disc can be smaller than the disc itself, since it stays hidden, so I'll aim for a round box about 110 mm across. I'm also checking the ESP32 layout: the board is about 63 mm long with the USB port at one short end, and I need to work out whether the 4.8 mm figure means the port sits flush or sticks out past the board edge.

I'm weighing whether the 4.8 mm figure means the USB port sticks out past the ESP32 board's edge or sits recessed inside it. The 7.53 mm gap to the perfboard edge and the board's 63.17 mm length don't quite add up to the perfboard's 70 mm, so I'm checking which end overhangs.

I'm checking whether the USB port's 4.8 mm figure means the port pokes past the ESP32 edge or sits recessed, since that sets how far the plug mouth sits inside the perfboard edge. If the port protrudes, the opening is about 2.7 mm in, and if it's recessed, about 12.3 mm in, so the wall opening has to clear the plug either way.

I'm checking whether the USB-C overmold would clear the ESP32 board if the port is recessed rather than protruding, since the board underside sits close to where the plug body would be.

I'm wondering whether the USB port really overhangs the ESP32 edge by 4.8 mm, since that seems large for a DevKitC-style board, though it may still be workable. I could ask the user for one clarifying measurement, and I also still need to know which side of the perfboard the ESP32 sits on, plus where the input wires leave the disc and how tall the disc-side components are.

I'm now planning where the input wires leave the disc, whether at the edge or nearer the centre, and I'll need the connector's radius from the centre to settle that. I'm also assuming 1.6 mm for both the perfboard and the disc, and laying out the perfboard holes at 2.4 mm diameter, 0.9 mm from the edges, which gives 65.8 × 45.8 mm spacing for M2 self-tapping screws into 1.7 mm pilot holes.

I'm now settling how the box splits into parts: a tray with the back and walls, and a front lid that the disc screws onto. Mounting the perfboard on the lid and hanging the tray on the wall would let me fasten the tray screws from inside before attaching the lid, and I'd need to cut the USB port opening into the tray wall.

I'm sketching out how the keyholes fit with the perfboard: the screw heads will stick into the box about 3 mm, so the keyholes need to sit outside the perfboard footprint to keep clear of the solder joints. I also need to work out how the keyhole head pocket prints on the bed, since the slot will need a bridge across the top.

I'm settling the keyholes: a 10 mm entry hole with a 4.8 mm slot running upward from it, so the box slides down onto the screw shanks. The screw heads sit about 3 mm inside the back plate, so there's no bridge needed. I'm also checking how the lid fastens to the tray.

I'm settling the lid's fastening: M3 screws go through the lid into heat-set inserts in the tray bosses, and the heads need counterbores so they don't push the disc off. I'm also checking the counterbore printing, since the step down to the narrower hole is a short overhang that may need a sacrificial layer, or I could print the lid face-up instead.

I'm thinking about how to get the lid's insert holes to work. The lid needs bosses on its inside face for the disc inserts, and since bosses can't print easily face-up, I'm printing the lid face-down so the holes open from the bed side into the bosses.

I'm settling the lid's insert holes and screw lengths: the disc screws are M3 heads on the LED side, so I'd go with M3x6 to get about 4.4 mm of engagement into an insert set in a boss inside the lid. The lid prints face-down so those bosses rise up and the hole is blind with a ceiling at the top, and the counterbores for the lid screws open from the bed side.

I'm working out where the disc's input wires leave the disc and whether the connector sits near the edge or closer to the centre. I'm also thinking about a box that's round, roughly 130 mm across, with the perfboard inside and the ESP32's USB port facing down so the charger cable hangs below.

I'm weighing whether the port should sit at the bottom of the round box, where the wall is perpendicular to the port. I'd need to know how far the ESP32 sits off the perfboard's centreline, so I'll batch that with the other measurements I'm missing. On depth, I'm working out about 26 mm of interior, since the standoffs, the board and the ESP32 height add up from the back face.

I'm checking whether the perfboard's port end can sit close enough to the round wall: at the 50 mm width the inner wall curves in to about 57.8 mm, so the port edge needs roughly 5 mm of clearance there, plus the 2.7 mm mouth inset, which puts the plug opening about 7.7 mm from the inner wall.

I'm settling on a rounded rectangle instead of a cylinder, since it's hidden behind the disc anyway and the flat bottom gives the port a clean wall to work with. I'm checking the perfboard edge against the inner wall there, which leaves about 4.2 mm from the plug mouth to the wall.

I'm checking whether the overmold can clear the wall opening and still sit above the perfboard, since the plug mouth sits about 12 mm in, so I'll make the cutout generous with a chamfer. I still need to confirm whether the USB port overhangs the ESP32 board edge.

I need to ask for the disc's wire connector location and whether there are components on the back of the disc, so I'm bundling those two questions with the earlier measurements into one batch.
